## Santa Teresa: Rio de Janeiro's Bohemian Neighbourhood

We offer a jeep tour, or you can take the rattling single-car tram to Santa Teresa, Rio de Janeiro's bohemian quarter, sometimes called Brazil's "Montparnasse". The tram travels through green tropical forest, with views of Rio de Janeiro along the way.

The neighbourhood has preserved its old colonial houses amid lush greenery. You will find numerous cosy cafés, street musicians and small shops here.

Today, Santa Teresa has become an arts hub, with many artists' studios displaying paintings. The artists are happy to discuss their work if you speak English or with your guide's help. You can buy a painting here or commission one.

Afterwards, you return on the same tram to the station and travel from there to the foot of Mount Corcovado. A small train then carries you through tropical trees towards your destination.

A few minutes' walk from the station brings you to the foot of the impressive Christ the Redeemer statue (Cristo Redentor). Enjoy beautiful views of Rio de Janeiro, take photographs and listen to your guide's account of how this extraordinary monument was created.

The route continues to Puna Pau, a scenic volcanic area where red tuff was quarried in ancient times. This stone was used to make pukao, the distinctive stone headdresses placed on the heads of some moai.

Next, you will visit the Tahai ceremonial complex, one of Rapa Nui's most important archaeological sites. The complex includes three main platforms: Ko Te Riku, where a moai's eyes have been restored, Tahai and Vai Uri.

At Ahu Akivi stand 7 moai, associated in local legend with the island's first scouts. Red tuff was quarried at Puna Pau to make the statues' head ornaments. The route then continues to the Tahai ceremonial complex with restored platforms, including Ko Te Riku with reconstructed eyes.

lead: The full-day Easter Island excursion begins on the south coast, visiting the unrestored Ahu Vaihu platform at Hanga Te'e Bay and Ahu Akahanga. According to legend, this is the burial place of the legendary King Hotu Matu'a. You then head to the Rano Raraku volcano, an ancient quarry where almost all the island's moai were carved. Around 397 statues remain on its slopes, while the island has approximately 900 moai in total. The next stop is Ahu Tongariki, Rapa Nui's largest restored ceremonial platform, where 15 magnificent moai stand in a row.

The route then continues to Ahu Te Pito Kura and the famous Te Pito o Te Henua stone, or "Navel of the World", regarded by local people as one of the island's most powerful energy sites. The day ends at Anakena Beach, with its white sand, palm trees and warm turquoise water. Here you will find Ahu Nau Nau, one of the island's most picturesque archaeological sites. There will be time for a walk and a swim, as well as a private picnic overlooking the coast.
